description:
Find players who scored 30+ runs in at least 3 consecutive matches in the
  2024 season, with the date each streak started. The query and the sample
  data are in sql/ipl_streaks/. Each player in seed.sql is one case.

elements.name: The query returns each streak once, with its start date

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "ipl_streaks" tables and sample data
I run the "ipl_streaks" query
the result has the columns "player_name, streak_start_date"

the result is:

elements.name: The sample data catches a query that orders matches by match_id, not date

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "ipl_streaks" tables and sample data
I run the "ipl_streaks" query with "ORDER BY m.match_date, m.match_id" changed to "ORDER BY m.match_id"
the changed query misses the row starting "Neel Chatterjee, 2024-03-22"

elements.name: The sample data catches a query that forgets the season filter

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "ipl_streaks" tables and sample data
I run the "ipl_streaks" query with "WHERE m.season = 2024" changed to "WHERE m.season >= 2023"
the changed query adds the row starting "Arjun Pillai, 2023-05-14"

elements.name: The sample data catches a query that skips matches where the player did not bat

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "ipl_streaks" tables and sample data
I run the "ipl_streaks" query with "WHERE m.season = 2024" changed to "WHERE m.season = 2024 AND b.runs IS NOT NULL"
the changed query adds the row starting "Vihaan Rao, 2024-03-22"

elements.name: The sample data catches a query that does not count a score of exactly 30

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "ipl_streaks" tables and sample data
I run the "ipl_streaks" query with "WHERE runs >= 30" changed to "WHERE runs > 30"
the changed query misses the row starting "Aarav Menon, 2024-03-22"

elements.name: The sample data catches a query that needs more than three matches

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "ipl_streaks" tables and sample data
I run the "ipl_streaks" query with "HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3" changed to "HAVING COUNT(*) > 3"
the changed query misses the row starting "Ishaan Bhatt, 2024-03-24"

name: SQL scenario 2 - IPL batting streaks

description:
Find transfers where account A pays account B and B pays back a similar
  amount (within 10%) within 24 hours. The query and the sample data are in
  sql/round_trip_transfers/. Each block of seed.sql is one case.

elements.name: The query finds exactly the round trips in the sample data

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "round_trip_transfers" tables and sample data
I run the "round_trip_transfers" query
the result has the columns "original_txn_id, return_txn_id, account_a, account_b, amount_sent, amount_returned, pct_difference, hours_apart"
the result is:

elements.name: The sample data catches a query that treats exactly 24 hours as too late

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "round_trip_transfers" tables and sample data
I run the "round_trip_transfers" query with "r.txn_time <= o.txn_time + INTERVAL '24 hours'" changed to "r.txn_time < o.txn_time + INTERVAL '24 hours'"
the changed query misses the row starting "7, 8"

elements.name: The sample data catches a query that treats exactly 10% as too much

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "round_trip_transfers" tables and sample data
I run the "round_trip_transfers" query with "ABS(r.amount - o.amount) <= 0.10 * o.amount" changed to "ABS(r.amount - o.amount) < 0.10 * o.amount"
the changed query misses the row starting "7, 8"

elements.name: The sample data catches a query that measures 10% against the returned amount

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "round_trip_transfers" tables and sample data
I run the "round_trip_transfers" query with "0.10 * o.amount" changed to "0.10 * r.amount"
the changed query adds the row starting "26, 27"

elements.name: The sample data catches a query that lets the return come before the payment

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "round_trip_transfers" tables and sample data
I run the "round_trip_transfers" query with "(r.txn_time, r.txn_id) > (o.txn_time, o.txn_id)" changed to "r.txn_id <> o.txn_id"
the changed query adds the row starting "2, 1"

elements.name: The sample data catches a query that drops transfers that share a timestamp

steps.name: a fresh PostgreSQL database with the "round_trip_transfers" tables and sample data
I run the "round_trip_transfers" query with "(r.txn_time, r.txn_id) > (o.txn_time, o.txn_id)" changed to "r.txn_time > o.txn_time"
the changed query misses the row starting "22, 23"

name: SQL scenario 1 - round-trip transfers
